entities.summary:
Lucius Marius Maximus Perpetuus Aurelianus was a Roman biographer who wrote a series of biographies of twelve Emperors in the early decades of the 3rd century AD. His work, though lost, was still being read in the late 4th century and was used as a source by writers of that era, notably the author of the Historia Augusta. Marius's biographies aimed to imitate and continue the work of Suetonius, but their reliability and extent are still debated among scholars. 

Marius's significance lies in his contribution to the understanding of Roman history, particularly during the Late Empire period. His biographies provided valuable insights into the lives and reigns of twelve Emperors, offering a unique perspective on the politics, society, and culture of the time. 

The loss of Marius's work has led to a greater appreciation for the Historia Augusta, which drew heavily from his biographies. Scholars continue to study the Historia Augusta to gain a deeper understanding of the Late Empire period, and Marius's work remains an important part of this narrative. 

In conclusion, Marius Maximus Perpetuus Aurelianus's biographies of Emperors provide a fascinating glimpse into the history of the Late Empire, and his work continues to be relevant to scholars today.
